faq.q: Which khao soi on the Chiang Mai Michelin list should I try?
faq.a: Khao Soi Mae Sai is the name people mention most on the list, with soft noodles and a rich, deep curry broth. Go around midday before it sells out.

faq.q: Where do I go for real Northern Thai food?
faq.a: Huen Muan Jai and Huan Soontaree serve traditional Northern spreads, while Gongkham and Euang Kam Sai are local favorites for the same regional cooking.

faq.q: What are the cheapest Michelin picks in Chiang Mai?
faq.a: Street eats like Lung Khajohn Wat Ket, Sanpakoi Kanomjeen, and Roti Pa Day fill you up for pocket change, usually well under a hundred baht.

faq.q: How should a first-timer plan a Chiang Mai eating route?
faq.a: Start the morning with Khao Soi Mae Sai, snack around the Wat Ket area at Lung Khajohn Wat Ket, then close the day with a Northern spread at Huen Muan Jai or Huan Soontaree.

faq.q: Does Chiang Mai have any Michelin-starred restaurants?
faq.a: Not in 2026. Chiang Mai has no starred spots, but it carries 18 Bib Gourmand restaurants plus 18 Selected, making it a stronghold for great, affordable eating.
